feature: A track lists only what is animated
summary: Add Key no longer fills a clip's track with a row for Position, Scale, Rotation and Opacity. It puts one hollow diamond on the clip, and a value gets a row only once it has keys: change it on a layer with keys and it joins by itself; click a row's name and press Delete and it leaves; Animate on the clip's right-click brings one back.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open the sample recording and type a title over it with the Text tool.

try.do: Park the playhead at one second, right-click the title's clip and choose Add Key: one hollow diamond appears on the clip and no rows open under it.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Right-click the clip again and choose Animate > Scale: a Scale row appears and the hollow diamond fills.
Click the word Scale in the row's gutter: the row is picked.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Delete: the Scale row leaves and the title keeps its size. Press Command-Z to bring it back.
Right-click the diamond on the clip and choose Animate > Scale: the same list, from the key itself.
Move the playhead to three seconds and drag the title across the canvas: a Position row appears with a key at one second holding where it was and one at three where you left it.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Change the opacity in the panel at a new time: Opacity joins the same way, and Clip > Animate in the menu bar lists what is not animating yet.

evaluate: Does a hollow diamond read as a key with nothing in it yet, or does it look like a broken one?
Is clicking a row's name and pressing Delete the way you expected to stop animating something?
Does a change on a layer with keys keying itself feel right in practice, or do you find yourself making keys you did not mean?
Is Animate > Transform, 3D, Look, Effects the right shape for the list, or is it too long on a title?
rough: No mock covers a key on a clip's very first frame: there the hollow diamond sits on the trim grip like every other key does, and is harder to see than one mid clip.

Dragging on the canvas with a row picked does not yet move every key of that row, as the mock's interaction table and the card's mitigation say it should: dragging-on-the-canvas-with-a-row-picked-moves-t.
The row's right-click Easing lists the same ways a key eases as a key's own menu, not the mock's ten curves and Draw a Curve: dragging-on-the-canvas-with-a-row-picked-moves-t carries it.

The clip's menu says Add Key at 0:01.00 rather than the mock's Add Key, because a right-click leaves the playhead parked and the row says where the key goes (your call on 2026-10-13, a right click never moves the playhead).

The Key at Playhead row in Clip > Animate now does what Add Key does on a layer with nothing animating (a hollow moment) rather than keying Position; the mock does not show that row, so it matches its Add Key.
